controls.title: Collect security events centrally
controls.statement: Collect relevant security events from in-scope systems in a central location, with enough detail to identify the actor, action, target and time.
controls.risk: An attack could remain unnoticed if important systems do not provide usable security records.
controls.scope: In-scope operating systems, applications and central log collection.
controls.examine: Compare the system inventory and required event types with collected sources, timestamps, event fields and collection failures.
controls.interview: Ask the collection owner how new systems and missing or malformed events are detected.
controls.test: Generate authorised benign events on sampled systems and trace complete records into central storage.
test_steps: Select critical systems and event types from the logging design and include authentication, privilege, configuration, network and security-tool activity.
Generate uniquely identifiable authorised events at each source and record the source time, actor, target, action and expected outcome.
Trace each event through collection and parsing into central storage, checking field accuracy, time synchronisation, duplication and end-to-end delay.
Interrupt one test log source or collector and verify monitoring detects the gap, alerts an owner and shows when complete collection resumes.
controls.expected: Required events reach central storage with usable information, and missing sources or collection failures are detected and resolved.

mappings.basis: Enable audit logging across the in-scope enterprise assets.
Centralise collection and retention to the extent possible.
Verify the security-relevant event set for macOS systems; a generic collection test alone is insufficient.
Verify the security-relevant event set for Linux systems.
Verify the security-relevant event set for Windows systems.

controls.title: Protect and retain security records
controls.statement: Restrict access and changes to security records and logging tools. Retain readable, searchable records for the required period.
controls.risk: Records that are altered, deleted or unavailable could prevent investigators from understanding an incident and identifying the harm caused.
controls.scope: Log stores, logging tools, authorised roles and retention requirements.
controls.examine: Inspect access rules, deletion controls, retention settings and oldest retrievable records.
controls.interview: Ask the log owner how access is approved, capacity is managed and attempts to alter records are handled.
controls.test: Use authorised test records and accounts to verify access and change restrictions. Retrieve records from the start of the required period and confirm they remain searchable and readable.
test_steps: Select current and oldest-required security records from different sources and compare actual storage tiers, retention dates and access with policy.
Using authorised read-only and unauthorised test identities, verify permitted search and export while alteration, deletion and configuration change are denied.
Create a test record with known content, follow any archive transition and retrieve it using normal investigation tooling to confirm readability and integrity.
Review privileged changes, deletion attempts and retention failures and confirm they are independently logged, alerted and investigated.
controls.expected: Unauthorised access, alteration and deletion are prevented; records remain usable throughout the applicable retention period.

mappings.basis: Protect event logs from unauthorised access.
Protect event logs from unauthorised modification and deletion.
Requires searchable retention for at least 12 months; verify actual availability over that period.
The source additionally requires alerts to designated roles when unauthorised access or changes are detected.
Requires at least 90 days of retention across enterprise assets; verify the full period and asset scope.

controls.title: Review security events and follow up suspicious activity
controls.statement: Review security events at the required frequency, investigate suspicious activity and track resulting decisions and actions.
controls.risk: Suspicious activity that is not investigated could continue unnoticed and cause greater damage to information and services.
controls.scope: Security monitoring responsibilities, log reviews and investigation records.
controls.examine: Review completed log analyses, alerts, investigation notes and recorded actions over the assessment period.
controls.interview: Ask analysts how suspicious activity is recognised, escalated and closed, and how priorities change when risk changes.
controls.test: Trace sampled relevant events into investigation and follow-up. Compare actual review dates with the required cadence and verify that findings reached the responsible people.
test_steps: Select high-risk detections, routine review items, false positives, escalated events and periods with no recorded findings.
Trace each source event through rule or review, analyst decision, enrichment, case creation, escalation and closure with required timestamps.
Reperform the decision using the available evidence and verify suppressed or closed events have a supported reason and authorised tuning where relevant.
Generate a benign event matching a selected detection and confirm timely alerting, assignment and follow-up by the responsible people.
controls.expected: Reviews are timely, relevant findings are investigated and communicated, and follow-up decisions and actions are evidenced.

mappings.basis: Requires log reviews at least weekly; verify the actual review cadence.
Also requires adjusting review activity when risk changes and defining review frequency and recipients.
